questions.question: What is a tax?
choices: A voluntary purchase of company stock
A required payment to government under law
A loan that must always be repaid to its payer
An insurance payment for private property

questions.question: What is an income tax based on?
choices: Taxable income
The distance between a home and a workplace
Only the value of imported goods
The number of elections held in a year

questions.question: What is a sales tax generally based on?
choices: The number of workers in a household
The assessed value of real estate
The amount of a bank loan's principal
The taxable value of a purchase

questions.question: What is a property tax commonly based on?
choices: The quantity of imported products
The amount of a worker's monthly wages
The assessed value of property
The interest rate on a savings account

questions.question: What is a progressive tax structure?
choices: One in which the share paid rises as the tax base increases
One in which everyone owes the same dollar amount
One applying only to purchases of imported goods
One collected only during economic recessions

questions.question: What is tax withholding from a paycheck?
choices: Money the worker borrows from the employer
Money sent to government toward the worker's tax obligations
A contribution that always buys company shares
A refund issued before any earnings are received

questions.question: What is an excise tax?
choices: A tax imposed only on inherited land
A tax that replaces every payroll contribution
A tax on a specified product or activity
A tax collected only by foreign governments

questions.question: Why do governments collect taxes?
choices: To guarantee every private business earns a profit
To prevent all households from saving
To replace every voluntary market transaction
To fund public services and other government responsibilities

questions.question: How does a tax deduction generally differ from a tax credit?
choices: A deduction reduces taxable income; a credit reduces tax owed
A deduction increases tax owed; a credit increases taxable income
Both always reduce tax owed by the same dollar amount
A deduction is available only after all taxes are refunded

questions.question: What does a marginal income tax rate apply to?
choices: Every dollar of all prior years' income
The next dollar of taxable income within the relevant bracket
Only the value of a household's land
The total cost of every taxable purchase

questions.question: Why can a flat sales tax take a larger share of a lower-income household's income?
choices: Lower-income households are always charged a higher sales-tax rate
All household spending is exempt from sales tax
Sales taxes are based only on annual income
Lower-income households may spend a larger share of income on taxed purchases

questions.question: What does a tax refund generally indicate?
choices: The taxpayer had no income during the year
The government is paying interest on every purchase
Payments and applicable refundable credits exceeded final tax liability
The taxpayer will never owe taxes in future years

questions.question: Why are some taxes placed on products such as tobacco?
choices: To raise revenue and potentially discourage consumption
To guarantee that everyone buys equal quantities
To remove the product from every tax base
To require sellers to offer the product without charge

questions.question: What is the difference between legal tax avoidance and tax evasion?
choices: Avoidance always involves false reporting; evasion never does
Avoidance uses lawful provisions; evasion illegally avoids obligations
Both describe any payment made before the deadline
Both are required methods of completing a tax return

questions.question: Why do many tax systems use several different tax bases?
choices: Different bases guarantee identical effects on all taxpayers
Only one tax can legally exist at each government level
Different bases remove the need for public budgets
They spread revenue collection across different economic activities and assets

questions.question: A taxable purchase costs $50 before a 6% sales tax. What is the total price?
In a simplified system, the first $10,000 of income is taxed at 10%, and the next $5,000 at 20%. What tax is owed on $15,000?
A taxpayer owes $800 before an applicable $200 nonrefundable tax credit. What tax remains?
A worker has $1,200 withheld but a final tax liability of $1,000, with no other adjustments. What is the result?
choices: An additional $200 owed
A $1,000 refund
A $200 refund
No payment or refund

questions.question: Two taxpayers owe the same $500 tax, but one earns $10,000 and the other $50,000. Which comparison is correct?
choices: The higher-income taxpayer pays a larger share of income
Both pay 5% of income
Both pay 1% of income
The lower-income taxpayer pays a larger share of income
